articles.title: FreeBSD GUS
articles.summary: FreeBSD's GUS is a safe memory reclamation scheme that uses a quiescent point to ensure memory is freed only after all CPUs have passed through a certain point, providing a barrier between threads and preventing concurrent access to potentially-freed memory. This is achieved through a combination of read and synchronize operations, which block quiescent points and inhibit preemption during read operations. The scheme is part of the Epoch-based reclamation family and has been described in detail by its author, Paul McKenney, in his LWN Articles.
